patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff did not apply to the vulnerable workspace checkout, so fixed-side validation used the authoritative `n132/arvo:23764-fix` image. That fixed image contains the moved `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;` guard before `c = data[i];`: the original PoC is clean there, the last selected `codefence_pre_read_guard` is guarded with `fence_skip_index_plus_two=5` and `fence_candidate_size=3`, and the adjacent `spaces_then_backticks_boundary` perturbation gives a genuine witness where the same selected path executes `codefence_read_sink` with `fence_candidate_size=6`.

root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: after skipping leading spaces, `i + 2 < size` must hold before `c = data[i]` is allowed to execute
root_cause_criterion.criterion: At the `is_codefence()` pre-read state immediately before `c = data[i];`, the parser must prove that three fence bytes remain in the candidate after the skipped leading spaces, i.e. `i + 2 < size`. When this predicate is false the read must be rejected before any `data[i]` dereference.
root_cause_criterion.description: AddressSanitizer identifies `c = data[i];` in `is_codefence()` as both the sink and the root-cause site. The missing source-level obligation is the moved fixed-image guard `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;`: on the vulnerable original the selected three-space candidate reaches the pre-read state with `i == size == 3`, so `i + 2 < size` is false and the read still executes; on the fixed original the same state is guarded, while the adjacent boundary case with three preserved spaces plus three appended backticks makes the predicate true and still executes the protected read.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original trace records `codefence_pre_read_guard.fence_skip_index_plus_two=5` and `codefence_pre_read_guard.fence_candidate_size=3`, followed by the protected `codefence_read_sink`, so the required assertion is violated there. The authoritative fixed original records the same `5` and `3` at `codefence_pre_read_guard` but no `codefence_read_sink`, so the required assertion is guarded. The nearest source-grounded perturbation `spaces_then_backticks_boundary` preserves the original three skipped spaces and appends the minimum three backticks needed to make `fence_candidate_size=6`, giving a genuine fixed-side witness with `5 < 6` and an executed `codefence_read_sink`.

nodes.state: At the vulnerable sink read, the selected `is_codefence()` candidate has `fence_skip_index >= fence_candidate_size`, so `c = data[i]` dereferences at or past the end of the current slice.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `codefence_read_sink.fence_skip_index=3` and `codefence_read_sink.fence_candidate_size=3`, satisfying the selected out-of-bounds relation `3 >= 3` on the crashing read.

edges.relation: The same post-skip index `i` that violates the missing pre-read guard is the index consumed unchanged by the later `c = data[i]` sink read.
edges.evidence: Both the vulnerable original and the `spaces_then_backticks_boundary` perturbation record `codefence_pre_read_guard.fence_skip_index == codefence_read_sink.fence_skip_index == 3`.

edges.relation: The exact fence-candidate length selected at `parse_listitem()` reaches `is_codefence()` unchanged as its `size` argument.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original records `fence_candidate_call.fence_candidate_size == codefence_pre_read_guard.fence_candidate_size == 3`, and `spaces_then_backticks_boundary` records the same propagation on `6`.
